mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility over the last two weeks indicates people are spending more time at home, which substitutes for and suppresses retail and recreation visits, pulling RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 11.7 at t-2w to 17.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL rising for two or more consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT mobility falls below -70 percent of baseline, it signals renewed public caution or restrictions on transit use consistent with rising infection concern, which spills over into reduced non-essential travel and lowers RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -70 for at least one of the last two weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at t-0w is -71.7, below the -70 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline (or rises) over the next 14 days following a weekly mean of TRANSIT below -70.

mechanism_narrative: Joint deterioration in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility reflects a broader pullback from commuting and in-person activity; because retail footfall is often linked to commute routes, the combined decline amplifies the drop in RETAIL_REC beyond what either series would predict alone over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES (-31.0) and TRANSIT (-71.7) worsened at t-0w relative to t-2w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall further than a single-series baseline model predicts when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT decline concurrently for two or more weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a pandemic-resurgence regime, elevated RESIDENTIAL (above +15) combined with declining WORKPLACES (below -25) indicates households are responding to renewed health risk by curtailing discretionary outings, which continues to depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks until the regime shifts.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above 15 and WORKPLACES below -25 simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at t-0w is 17.0 and WORKPLACES at t-0w is -31.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above 15 and WORKPLACES remaining below -25 throughout the period.

mechanism_narrative: During late summer, elevated PARKS mobility reflects a seasonal preference for outdoor recreation that substitutes for indoor retail and recreation visits; as long as PARKS remains meaningfully above its recent trough, RETAIL_REC stays suppressed relative to its own longer-run average over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 10 points week-on-week while RETAIL_REC simultaneously falls
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -36.7 at t-1w to -26.9 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC fell from -30.6 to -37.9 over the same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the same week that PARKS increases by more than 10 points, contradicting the proposed substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stayed close to baseline (near zero) while RETAIL_REC remains deeply negative and volatile, indicating the decline is concentrated in discretionary, non-essential retail activity rather than general mobility suppression; this discretionary-specific caution is expected to persist and keep RETAIL_REC low over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed within -5.4 to 1.3 while RETAIL_REC ranged from -47.4 to -21.3 over the same four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds toward baseline within one week even as GROCERY_PHARM remains flat near zero, indicating the discretionary-specific suppression mechanism does not hold.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown large week-to-week swings (e.g., a 26-point jump from t-3w to t-2w followed by declines), suggesting overreaction or noise rather than a stable trend; when such a large single-week swing occurs, a partial mean-reversion toward the recent four-week average is expected within one week.
candidate_trigger: absolute week-on-week change in RETAIL_REC exceeds 15 points
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC moved from -47.4 to -21.3 (t-3w to t-2w), a 26.1 point swing
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to move in the same direction as the prior large swing rather than reverting, over the next week.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of tightening pandemic-related restrictions, simultaneous declines in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT act jointly as a leading indicator of formal or informal policy responses (e.g., capacity limits, renewed advisories) that extend beyond individual behavior and suppress RETAIL_REC for a full four-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both decline for two consecutive weeks while RESIDENTIAL rises
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -20.4 to -31.0 and TRANSIT fell from -60.3 to -71.7 between t-2w and t-0w while RESIDENTIAL rose from 11.7 to 17.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next 28 days despite concurrent declines in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT alongside rising RESIDENTIAL.
